poiBE0-desc:
[{{title}}]

The year was 2070. Tensions between two Asian powers, having reached a boiling point, spilled over all too quickly.

International powers had no time to react and, before anyone knew it, a new Dark Age engulfed the world. The Age of Plenty was over.

The brief but deadly Pakistani-Indian War left an incredible footprint across the continent. Millions perished from famine, millions more were displaced. Soon the rest of the world felt the cold grip of ash. Economies collapsed. The satellites fell. The spirit of all nations was shaken.

But the Great Mistake did not end there. The lifestyle of modern societies, the exponential consumption of goods, the inability of people to look beyond tomorrow led to an even worse situation. The oceans swallowed entire cities. Societies enclosed on themselves, fighting wars of survival. The Earth, so close to globalization, fell far. The scars of bygone eons became visible once again. Hard times led to the development of new currents of thought, philosophies were forged to deal with the Great Mistake, with new technologies, with new problems.

But soon this era too will end. Civilizations across the world are awakening, one last time, to finish what they started, to bring balance to the world or to seek a second chance...

Beyond Earth
poiMIT-desc:
[{{title}}]

Based in Munich, German Federation, the Münchner Institut für Technologie—also known as Müninstek—was founded in the late 21st century with a mission to research and develop solutions to the world's most pressing environmental challenges. Its founders recognized the urgent need to address issues such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and resource depletion, and they believed that scientific research and technological innovation could help pave the way for a more sustainable future.

The Müninstek quickly became one of the world's leading institutions for research on global ecology and sustainability. Its scientists and engineers worked on a wide range of projects, from developing new renewable energy technologies to designing more efficient and sustainable transportation systems. The Müninstek also had a strong focus on environmental policy and worked closely with governments and international organizations such as the INTEGR to promote policies that would help mitigate the effects of climate change.

The INTEGR is a European-based political and social organization with its headquarters located in Germany. It pursues austerity and radical change to prevent global warming from making Earth uninhabitable. The organization recognizes the importance of scientific research and technological innovation in achieving its goals together with the Institute, and it worked closely with the Müninstek on a range of initiatives aimed at promoting sustainable development and mitigating the effects of climate change.

One of the Müninstek's most significant contributions was its development of the Ecomodel, a comprehensive tool developed by the Institute for measuring and analyzing the environmental impact of various human activities. The model takes into account a wide range of factors, including energy consumption, resource usage, emissions, waste generation, and other environmental impacts.

The model is continuously updated with new data and insights, allowing for more accurate assessments of environmental impact over time. It has become a crucial tool for policymakers, businesses, and researchers around the world who are working to promote sustainable development and mitigate the effects of climate change.

The Ecomodel enables comprehensive monitoring of the current state and potential evolution of the ecology in any given region. In order to effectively use this model, the Müninstek has developed a range of classifications that are based on the overall quality of the ecology in a particular territory and other complex criteria known as Local Ecobalance Decay Level—or LED.

Each of these classifications represents a different level of ecological health, and some are more rare than others. For example, achieving no or very low ecobalance decay is extremely difficult, and it is rare for any state to attain this level. However, some governments have been able to refine their ecological advocacy measures and instruments to a point where they can maintain a level of ecological balance that is close to optimal. In contrast, other governments may need to intervene more directly in order to protect their territories from negative ecological changes. This can involve using conventional ecological engineering techniques to terraform the land and create artificial barriers against environmental degradation.

Overall, the Ecomodel and the Müninstek classifications provide a valuable framework for understanding and managing the complex ecology of different regions. By using this model and its associated tools, governments and other stakeholders can work together to ensure that the environment is protected and preserved for future generations.
poiLYS-desc:
[{{title}}]

Lyscore—Lys, Science, Culture et Ouverture—is Franco-Iberia’s independent cultural and historical corporation, built to make humanity’s memory impossible to erase. Publicly chartered and funded through a combination of state investment and private partnerships, it operates at arm’s length from the government: accountable to the public, but free to decide what it preserves, how it investigates, and where its work takes it.

Its mandate is vast: to seek out, recover and safeguard the records of human civilization wherever they remain—in public collections, private hands, threatened archives, abandoned settlements or the digital debris of a vanished world. Documents, artworks, scientific findings, oral histories and everyday objects all belong in its care. Each acquisition is authenticated, catalogued and preserved, then added to a secure, continually expanding archive accessible across borders.

Lyscore was founded on a conviction born from catastrophe: history cannot warn us if its evidence is lost, hidden or forgotten. Preservation, in its view, is not enough. Knowledge must circulate. Through open archives, traveling exhibitions, public campaigns, research fellowships and international cultural summits, Lyscore brings the past into active conversation with the present—and puts its findings within reach of citizens, scholars and decision-makers alike.

To its supporters, Lyscore is a shared vault for the memory of humankind. To its critics, it is an institution with an extraordinary power to shape what the world remembers. It accepts the burden that comes with that power: to preserve without claiming ownership, to inform without dictating conclusions, and to keep humanity’s record alive—even when the truth it contains is uncomfortable.
poi001-desc:
[{{title}}]

The Catholic Church was once the largest religious group in the world throughout the past several centuries. It has had a history of splits, rivalries and rebellions, including the Great Schism, which led to the creation of the Orthodox Churches, and the Protestant Reformation, which established several new reformed churches such as Lutherans, Calvinists, and Presbyterians, to name a few. Despite the events of the past, the Catholic Church still stood strong in the world, triumphing over almost every obstacle it faced. But once again, the history repeats itself. Catholicism splits once more.

The Old Papacy, located in South America, claims to be the true spearhead of what the Church was always supposed to mean: humanity and solidarity, while keeping Catholic teachings alive and a decentralized power structure.

The New Papacy, located in the reborn, historical city of Avignon, has always made the effort of overcoming change while keeping its conservative values and centralized power structure. It has come under scrutiny and criticism for being the most stagnant branch of the Church in an effort to keep the traditional idea of the Church alive, favouring the ruling elite and accepting the patronage and assistance of leaders favourable to this entity, while also criticising the Old Papacy for not being true Catholics.

This has been known as the Second Great Schism.
poi002-desc:
[{{title}}]

The first version of the Eurotunnel was completed in 1994, more than two centuries ago, crossing the English Channel and thus linking the former France and the old United Kingdom.

It was the longest stretch of underwater railway in the world, allowing crossing from the continent to the island in less than 40 minutes. The machinery used in its construction amounted to 1,100 tonnes, with the capacity to drill 20 kilometres without interruption. 16 billion euros from private companies financed the project.

But the progress of science and of these European powers made it possible to develop drilling techniques far more effective than any that had got before. Thanks to the progress of the Scottish mining industry, cooperating with the English government and largely with funding from France—later Franco-Iberian—a much larger capacity tunnel was completed: the Third Millennium Eurotunnel.

This tunnel has the capacity for four maglev rail tracks, two in each direction, and a four-space motorway. Millions of people travel through these tunnels every month, connecting the two countries as never before.

If you are interested in travelling from Oxford to Paris you can get a maglev ticket now, it won't take more than an hour.

In fact if you think deeply about it, it would take you more time packing up than actually travelling!
poi003-desc:
[{{title}}]

Known as the The Swiss Plebiscite and taking place in the year 2107, Old Switzerland was split between Old Italy, France, and Germany through a combination of economic and political pressures. Despite famines and economic shortcomings, Switzerland proper remained largely unaffected by the Great Mistake, making it the envy of the crippled powers of Europe.

During the Dark Age, many extraterrestrial projects were abandoned due to a lack of funding, with the Mars Tragedy being the most well-known. The WCRB-Lua Moon Colony was founded by the Swiss as a tourist destination in 2074. Old flight plans put the colony's population at roughly 40 people. Post-Mistake rescue attempts were seen as unfeasible and, for most of the 22nd century, the colony was thought lost forever.

However, German scientists have recently noticed subtle signs that WCRB-Lua has survived. Some parts of the scientific community have argued that the colonists must have survived in stasis, while others have dismissed the notion as mere conjecture.

Fortunately, due to high popular support for the expedition, and to test humanity's spaceborne capacities, the German Federation has authorized the Roter-Mond Mission. Scheduled to be carried out next month, international treaties have already been signed to avoid complications and INTEGR sympathizers worldwide have convened to express their support. The Swiss region itself, an autonomous part of Germany, is planning a nation-wide celebration. Thousands are expected to attend and watch the operation unfold.
poiFRA-desc:
[{{title}}]

Franco-Iberia stands as a testament to the resilience and adaptability of human civilization in the face of catastrophe. Born from the fractured remnants of the Old European Union, it is more than just a nation—it is a symbol of unity forged through adversity.

While Europe avoided the most immediate devastation of the Great Mistake, it was soon overwhelmed by the ripple effects of global upheaval. Massive waves of refugees fleeing the chaos in Asia reshaped the continent, straining resources and exposing deep divides within the Old Union. Disagreements over priorities—whether to address the humanitarian crisis or prepare for environmental threats—splintered the fragile alliance. In the end, these pressures proved insurmountable, and the Old Union collapsed under the weight of its internal conflicts.

It can be said, and it is said, that Franco-Iberia is the spiritual child of the former European Union. While its territorial claims seem to indicate that its goal is to dominate the continent once and for all, some of its leaders are still squabbling over how to approach it.

One of the country's most important components is the Mediterranean Sea, which is essential for the Union's exports, with important trading partners such as Padania, Greece and even the Maghreb. Still, important emerging powers want to unseat Franco-Iberia from its position of economic hegemony, clashing head-on with the government's agenda.
FRApoi001-desc:
[{{title}}]

Franco-Iberia’s territorial ambitions and strategic positioning make it the spiritual successor to the Old European Union, but its vision is bolder and its methods more direct. With its sweeping claims over the western and southern parts of the continent, the Union aspires to establish itself as the unchallenged leader of Europe. Yet, internal tensions persist. Even decades after its inception, leaders within Franco-Iberia’s sprawling bureaucracy grapple with conflicting ideologies—from those advocating pan-European integration to hardliners intent on consolidating regional power at the expense of its neighbors.
FRApoi002-desc:
[{{title}}]

However, this economic hegemony does not go unchallenged. Emerging powers, emboldened by new technologies and alliances, are eager to undermine Franco-Iberia’s dominance. To the north, the North Sea Alliance—a coalition of Scandinavian nations—wields its growing influence over polar trade routes, siphoning off lucrative markets once reliant on Mediterranean access. To the east, the Eurasian Federation consolidates its economic and military might, posing an existential threat to Franco-Iberia’s ambitions. Even the Maghreb, long seen as a subordinate trading partner, is rising in prominence, driven by advancements in renewable energy and agricultural innovation, challenging Franco-Iberia’s control over southern trade corridors.
FRApoi003-desc:
[{{title}}]

Nobody in Franco-Iberia chose the phrase. It appeared on its own, first in the harbour taverns of Marseille and Neo Barcelona, and then everywhere: the Romans are back. A dockworker says it when a new customs tower rises over a Mediterranean port. A Padanian merchant mutters it over his ledgers when a Union tariff changes. In Athens it is said with a shrug, in Casablanca with a smirk, and in Berlin with a sneer.

It began as a joke and stopped being one. The comparisons are too easy to resist: a Senate that votes on everything, fortified ports, maglev lines laid where the old roads ran, a Mediterranean treated as a private lake, and an open conviction that the educated West has a duty to carry high culture to everyone else. Franco-Iberia has never claimed the title of empire, and nobody who uses the phrase believes it.

Over time it also became a name for the place itself. People speak of living under the Romans or beyond the Romans, the way their ancestors once spoke of the frontier of an older empire. A shipping route that crosses Union waters is the Roman leg. A town that has quietly adopted Union currency and Union schoolbooks has gone Roman. Franco-Iberians have taken the phrase back as well: Élodie’s admirers say it as a toast, and Al-Hakim’s followers say it as an accusation.

As the year 2200 unfolds, the question is no longer whether the phrase is fair but how the story ends. Rome took centuries to build and longer to fall, and the people who say it most cheerfully are seldom the ones who have read the last chapter. Franco-Iberia’s ability to adapt, innovate and persevere may yet keep it a formidable force on the global stage. But the legions of history had their own bureaucrats squabbling over the frontier, too.
FRApoi004-desc:
[{{title}}]

Long wealthy, Élodie's lineage traces back to the nobility and privileged elite of Old France, extending a millennium before the Great Mistake. Her family's prestige and influence stemmed not from peerage but from the vast fortune amassed over the prior two centuries through holdings in agriculture, food processing, pharmaceuticals, and textiles.

Élodie entered the world at Europe's foremost fertility and maternity clinic in Braga as the only child of her parents. Raised in opulence along the Côte d'Azur and Costa del Sol, she became a media darling during her teenage years, though not always in a favorable light. Critics labeled her an isolationist and a European elitist, a reputation bolstered by her famously sharp tongue and incisive wit.

A staunch advocate of Western cultural traditions, Élodie believed it was the duty of the educated European elite to guide the masses, ensuring the preservation of high culture. She viewed the independence and sustainability of the new Union as the best means to achieve this vision.
FRApoi005-desc:
[{{title}}]

Franco-Iberia is undergoing a profound cultural renaissance, a revival reminiscent of the Renaissance and Enlightenment eras it holds dear. This resurgence is not merely about preserving the great artistic achievements of the past but fostering a dynamic environment for new generations of creators to explore and innovate. Through the Programe Artistice National, the Union has launched ambitious initiatives to nurture emerging artists and authors, encouraging them to build on its rich traditions while exploring new horizons in art and thought.

From the quietest rural villages to the busiest urban centers, citizens are drawn to newly opened museums, theaters, and cinemas, celebrating both heritage and contemporary creativity. European works, enriched by cultural infusions from North Africa, have become a source of unifying pride. The Union's Directorate-General for Education and Culture actively promotes and exports this vibrant culture, spreading its influence across the globe through media and other channels.

In this flourishing environment, the Union's guiding ethos—trésors de l'esprit—remains clear: a person's true wealth lies in the knowledge and culture they carry and share, not in material accumulation. It is little wonder that, amid uncertainty and upheaval, many seek to join Franco-Iberia, drawn by its stability and dedication to the arts.
FRApoi006-desc:
[{{title}}]

The Mediterranean Sea, transformed by climate change but still vital, is the lifeblood of Franco-Iberia’s economy. Now a vast inland ocean with expanded shorelines, it serves as a crucial artery for trade and commerce. The nation’s ports, fortified and modernized, are hubs of activity, channeling goods and resources to and from key trading partners such as the industrial powerhouse of Padania to the northeast, the revitalized city-states of Greece, and the resource-rich but politically fragmented Maghreb to the south. Franco-Iberia’s dominance over Mediterranean trade routes is a cornerstone of its wealth and influence, allowing it to maintain a level of prosperity that few other nations can rival in this new world order.
FRApoi007-desc:
[{{title}}]

Franco-Iberia is governed by the Union Senate, a cornerstone of its democratic system, which deliberates and votes on all national matters. Esteemed worldwide as a model of effective democracy, the Senate fosters stability and a deep sense of civic engagement among its citizens. Direct votes from the populace are seamlessly processed through advanced computing systems, enabling efficient and transparent elections that strengthen public trust in the Union's governance.
FRApoi008-desc:
[{{title}}]

Al-Hakim is one of the most influential figures in the French political landscape. Born to an Algerian immigrant family in the now-flooded suburb of Saint-Ouen, North Paris, he grew up in the high-crime neighborhoods of the city. As a young man, he became involved in the criminal underworld. However, government initiatives aimed at reforming at-risk youth recognized Al-Hakim's potential and offered him opportunities to change his path.

Determined to rebuild his life, Al-Hakim immersed himself in economics, philosophy, and history. By the age of 23, he had written his first book, marking the beginning of a widely popular literary career. His success culminated in the release of the controversial yet best-selling Hakim Manifesto. The book, known for its sharp critique of 21st-century culture and lifestyles, blamed societal decline on a group he labeled the seres faux, while advocating for the empowerment of the seres vrais. Although historians dismissed the book as lacking scholarly rigor, its message resonated deeply with the people of Franco-Iberia.

Buoyed by widespread public support, Al-Hakim used his newfound wealth to establish the Partido Populaire, which quickly became the second most powerful political force in Franco-Iberia. His movement continues to attract a growing base of followers, driven by his promises of reform and social justice.

Ultimately, Al-Hakim envisions a future of complete social equality and comprehensive political restructuring, striving to ensure that the seres faux never regain influence over society.
poiGER-desc:
[{{title}}]

The German Federation acts as the spearhead of an important environmental movement under the acronym INTEGR, short for Initiative für Nachhaltige Technologien, Effizienz, Gerechtigkeit und Rechtschaffenheit, the Initiative for Sustainable Technologies, Efficiency, Justice and Righteousness. It is spreading throughout Europe, especially in neighboring countries such as Czechia and Poland.

Germany's leaders use this political platform to achieve governance. They differ sharply in their objectives and even more in their methods, yet three things hold them together: the Ecomodel, which gives every faction the same numbers to argue over; the shared fear of a second Great Mistake; and a common opponent in Franco-Iberia. INTEGR does not only focus on environmental issues, but also has positions on social and political issues, and its popularity has exploded in recent years.

The movement was born in the shadow of the Great Mistake. As the Old European Union fractured over whether to feed the refugees or fortify the coasts, INTEGR offered a third answer: that both crises had one root, and that the continent could survive only by changing how it lived. Its founders argued that the Dark Age was not an accident but a bill coming due, and that every year of delay would make it larger.

Its programme rests on austerity and radical change. Member governments accept strict limits on consumption, energy use and land development, and in return INTEGR offers them something the rest of Europe lacks: a shared plan. Policy is guided by the Ecomodel of the Müninstek, and territories are expected to meet the targets it sets or face the intervention of the movement's directives. A directive is INTEGR's basic unit: a national branch or ideological current with its own mandate, leadership and reading of the programme, bound to the others by the Ecomodel's targets rather than by a single party line. Positions on social and political questions therefore vary from directive to directive.

Critics, chiefly in Franco-Iberia, call the movement a green authoritarianism, accusing it of using the climate emergency to justify rationing, surveillance and the erosion of national sovereignty. Supporters answer that the oceans have already swallowed entire cities, and that sovereignty means little on a drowned coast. Whoever is right, the movement shows no sign of slowing, and its slogan can be read on walls from the Baltic to the Danube: Europe will be green, or it will not be at all.
GERpoi001-desc:
[{{title}}]

Born in Berlin to a German diplomat and a Polish teacher, Lena was raised as a child of the world. Over the course of 15 years, she lived on four continents and learned to speak eight languages.

Lena fought fearlessly for refugee rights throughout central and eastern Europe. Her early work at the Braungart-Wissel Foundation for Environmental Law garnered her acclaim, and she was soon seen as an emerging leader of sustainability and the environmental policymaking. As she became a prominent lawyer-activist in post-Mistake Europe, Lena was an increasingly easy target for Franco-Iberian politicians. Painted as a desperate anarchist, Lena's non-traditional lifestyle and worldview was frequently highlighted in order to polarize moderates. It was Lena's suggestions for radical measures in everything from economic and environmental policy to urban planning and foreign affairs that underlined the difference between the old fashioned imperials of Franco-Iberia and the new techno-green ideology of INTEGR.

It wasn't until Lena's most vocal and harshest critic—and cousin—Élodie, began her campaign for Franco-Iberian politics that Lena's vision for a transmodernist society crystallized. Transmodernism meant xenophily, globalism, and a place for both tradition and modernity.
GERpoi002-desc:
[{{title}}]

For untold millennia, humanity has lived in harmony with the environment around it, taking what is necessary and giving back what it can.

To Eva Rosenfeld, life is complicated but doesn't need to be as complicated as it is. She initially studied to be a Historian, absorbing recounts of events long since passed, eventually climbing to be a Professor of History at the University of Leipzig. Everything from prehistory, to the birth of civilisation in Mesopotamia, and the middle ages became her drive, even studying what has been affectionately titled the Age of Plenty of humanity which brought forth immense technological growth as well as its most insufferable, ecological hubris. Years of studying humanity in its most natural state contrasted with the dying artificial state it has now suspended itself in, then broke the hopeful scholar.

Drowning in grief, she began writing her Magnum Opus, the culmination of her new worldview, The Rights of the Earth. The academic community panned it as unscientific and more of a manifesto. Franco-Iberia restricted its import and struck it from school reading lists, which only widened its audience, and after the Green Soil plan, Polish and Czech ministries adopted it as a school reader. A generation of children is will be growing up on her words.

Now an official affiliate with INTEGR, Prof. Rosenfeld thus champions an agrarian and simplistic lifestyle, free from the crooked nature of industrial life, a life in touch with the spirit of the land and its creatures. Although many question her state of mind, it is without doubt her thoughts have strung a chord with the people.
GERpoi003-desc:
[{{title}}]

Of the INTEGR faction, few are as calculated and collected as the elusive Eugen Langer. A certified genius and researcher from the Berlin Research Institute, Eugen prefers to observe the world through a very specific wavelength.

Initially beginning as a chemistry student, Langer's academic life exploded into numerous fields of research, eventually collecting himself 5 PhDs, and publishing more than 30 papers in fields such as Particle Physics, Organic Chemistry and Bioengineering. Renowned for his intellect and feared for his cold attitude towards others, he made few friends during this period of his life, instead sticking close to immediate family.

Sadly however, a brutal blow would be dealt to this stability. Langer watched as his father, his most cherished friend and only remaining parent, died painfully from a treatable infection of the lungs. Discovering that budget cuts had been made to the health department for the sake of increased welfare payments, his formerly stoic and logical mind was brought to anger and frustration.

To Langer, the democratic system was revealed to be a paper-thin façade for the ineptocratic mess that was led by a weak and imprudent mass mentality, incapable of leading humanity into the future. INTEGR was therefore the best alternative, a group of alternate-thinking individuals who see that a shift in gear is necessary to prepare for the future. Joining at the first opportunity, his systematic diligence and hard work paid off, forming his own Sophistocratic faction, idolising a scholar-led society.

Langer does not oppose austerity. He is its most rigorous defender. What enraged him was that the knife fell on hospitals while welfare grew, and in his view the problem was never the cut but the hand holding it. While Langer is certainly no politician, his branch of INTEGR is understandably the most feared for having a true genius at the helm.
GERpoi004-desc:
[{{title}}]

Lena Ebner represents a watershed moment in the history of post-Mistake Europe. An event of this magnitude occurs only once a generation. Billed as a response to the new imperialism, what this actually means is nothing less than a cogent new political philosophy, neither right nor left, dominionist nor green.

Its defining feature is a strong posture against Franco-Iberia's agenda. Its appeal reaches well beyond Germany, including into the refugee districts and working suburbs of its neighbouring countries.
GERpoi005-desc:
[{{title}}]

The aristocratic spirit of seriousness and ancien régime of Western rationalistic technocracy have motivated the politics of this age, with the agents of the state and entertainment serving as gatekeepers for what is good and what is bad for the people.

Transmodernism means xenophily, globalism, and a place for both tradition and modernity.
GERpoi006-desc:
[{{title}}]

Green Austerity is INTEGR's central programme: every territory receives a consumption and emissions allowance set by the Ecomodel, tiered by its Local Ecobalance Decay, and is expected to live within it. Territories that overshoot face the intervention of the directives, from rationing to direct oversight of land use.

The programme owes much to Lena Ebner, who bridged the gap between technocrat, activist, and environmentalist and suggested the Party restructure its organization under those three verticals. Her proposals for radical measures, from economic policy to urban planning, turned austerity from a sacrifice into a plan, and gave INTEGR a coherent answer to the Franco-Iberian model.
GERpoi007-desc:
[{{title}}]

Poland and Czechia were not affected by the Great Mistake with the same intensity as other countries or their own neighbour, the German Federation. For this reason the Green Soil plan was signed by these three countries in 2194 with the aim of maintaining a dynamic, mutually supportive and green economy.

Since then, relations between the three countries have only improved. In all three, the Initiative has great social support and is seen as the future of the region and of Europe as a whole.

The reality is that this treaty has led to an interdependence between the signatory countries, where if the economy of one were to fall, the economies of the others would be seriously affected. That is why the engagement between these countries will be long-lasting and prosperous, as long as the ambitions of European leaders do not get in the way.
GERpoi008-desc:
[{{title}}]

Eva Rosenfeld's book argues that forests, rivers and coastlines should hold standing of their own, with guardians who can speak for them before a court. Humanity, she writes, is a tenant on the planet and not its owner, and every law should be read with that in mind.

Historians call it poetry rather than science, and they are not entirely wrong. But lawyers such as Lena Ebner saw a framework hiding inside the lyricism, and several INTEGR directives have since written ecosystem guardianship into their statutes.

The book has been banned from Franco-Iberian classrooms, where the Directorate-General for Education and Culture calls it a sentimental tract. In Poland and Czechia it is a school reader. Few texts show the split in Europe more clearly than where it is taught and where it is not.
GERpoi009-desc:
[{{title}}]

Eugen Langer's doctrine holds that a society can be governed well only by those who understand the systems they govern. Under his model the electorate chooses the goals, but the means, such as budgets, quotas and the allocation of cuts, are decided by a council of examined experts, chosen through open tests in the disciplines the Ecomodel relies on.

Opponents call it an aristocracy of the credentialed. Langer answers that nobody votes on who performs the surgery. His critics in Franco-Iberia have also noticed a resemblance to Élodie's belief in the duty of the educated elite to guide the masses, which Langer rejects with some heat: her elite is born, his is examined, and anyone willing to study may join.

Of all INTEGR's currents, Sophistocracy is the one that frightens its own allies. It makes no promise to be popular, only to be right.
GERpoi010-desc:
[{{title}}]

In the winter of 2088, a storm surge broke through the Elbe defences and Hamburg was underwater within a week. Thousands died, and hundreds of thousands fled south into a Germany already crowded with refugees from Asia. The Old European Union's emergency council spent that winter deadlocked over whether to feed the displaced or fortify the coasts.

In the spring of 2089, a coalition of coastal municipalities, refugee-aid activists and scientists of the Müninstek met in Munich and signed the founding charter of INTEGR. The Müninstek supplied the first Ecomodel projections, which showed that without drastic limits, more cities would follow within a generation. That single finding became the movement's argument.

For years INTEGR was dismissed as a movement of doom-sayers. Then the Old Union collapsed, and its directives turned out to be the only governments in Europe with a plan. The slogan came later, first printed on a poster pasted over the ruins of Hamburg harbour: Europe will be green, or it will not be at all.
poiNAU-desc:
[{{title}}]

The North American Union is a country in name far more than in practice. Central, the government that emerged from the Siege of Washington in 2084, still speaks for the Union abroad, signs its treaties and holds its seat among the nations. At home, its authority barely reaches past its own district. The rest of the Union is carved into numbered Districts, each with its own cliques, militaries and loyalties. On paper they all belong to a Greater American Identity that also embraces Canada and Mexico. In practice most of them pay Central nothing beyond lip service.

Central's great rival is ARC, the American Reclamation Corporation. It began as a government contractor, sent in to rescue and resettle populations after the disasters that followed the Great Mistake. Over the decades that work earned it the loyalty, the capital and the checkpoints that Central never managed to keep. Today some Districts answer to Central, some to ARC, some to both at once, and some to neither. Where ARC governs, it governs like a company: with oversight boards, research mandates and a close eye on the quarterly returns of rejuvenation technology.

Older powers linger beneath both. The United Nations clings to life in New England, the remnants of the pre-war warlords and the Chrysalids still prowl the West, and everywhere there are tribes, raiders and refugee towns that predate the Union and expect to outlast it. Few of them recognize anyone's right to rule.

Now the Union faces a crisis of succession. President Cygan will not seek another term, and the Central Council, an unofficial sea of politicians, lobbyists, officers and spies, must choose his successor. The Joint Chiefs will have the last word. Whoever wins inherits a Union held together by whoever is strongest in the room, and in the year 2200 nobody is quite sure who that is.
NAUpoi001-desc:
[{{title}}]

After the Siege of Washington in 2084, where the military forced the pre-Mistake government into exile in order to break the political deadlock that only exacerbated the chaos gripping the country from disasters and militia violence, the Central government was never truly able to fulfill their promise of restoring the government. Even though all three of the pre-Mistake branches are present, it's only the Executive that has any practical ability to pass policy, and even they are beholden to the Joint Chiefs. This has led to the military often being described as The Fourth Branch—mostly by anti-Central factions lambasting it as a glorified military dictatorship, but occasionally by members of the Central military who feel they deserve the political influence they wield for protecting democracy.
NAUpoi002-desc:
[{{title}}]

While the many Districts disagree, often violently, they have one agreement in common; Central is the worst. Even citizens living within the region the Central government directly controls hate them, to the point that the military police cannot contain the rising protest movements. Whoever the Central Council appoints as President, they will need to deal with the protestors... one way, or another.
NAUpoi003-desc:
[{{title}}]

The provinces once known as California are fried. Just like its East Coast counterpart, the land is heavily flooded and has a bloody history of anarchy. The few who remain live their lives as raiders, pillaging long-abandoned homes and farms in a never-ending search for food. Scars from meltdowns and chemical warfare still plague the air.
NAUpoi004-desc:
[{{title}}]

District 2 has been fighting the subversive Chrysalids for some time now. As the last remnants of pre-war warlords, the enigmatic Silk Path has continued to be a thorn in the side of both Central and ARC. District 2's officers are tasked with cleansing the District of the subversives… but may have other plans waiting in store.
NAUpoi005-desc:
[{{title}}]

District 2 is ruled by two organizations simultaneously.

The first is the ARC Delegation, led by Vice President Antony Beaton of Reclamation Cascadia. Although far away from home, this clique has managed to secure a support base among the District's affluent citizenry. Due to its mountainous nature, old Cascadia has escaped the worst of the Great Mistake, which has allowed it to keep a sizable middle class, which is all too eager to support Beaton's promises of extended life.

The other faction, led by Relief Officer Haven Barnett, is the Central Delegation. While it draws popular backing from the poorer Southern parts, it has roots in the upper classes as well. Though less radical than her ARC counterpart, Barnett also seeks the elusive goal of extended life.

For now, the two factions are united in the struggle against the Western warlord. But as victory draws closer, the cracks deepen, and the whole structure can come crashing down...
NAUpoi006-desc:
[{{title}}]

The land once known as the East Coast is dead and buried under the sea. Following the Great Mistake, the entire populations of New York, Boston, and other ancient metropoli fled for the Midwest. As expected, the unstable Federal government was unable to deal with mass migration and buckled in the 2nd American Civil War. Famine set in. Families turned into gangs and friends killed friends just for a slice of meat. So it continues to this day. The East Coast is in complete anarchy. The only authority comes from ARC's enforcers, who have fortified checkpoints and refugee camps, bringing some semblance of order to the wastes.
NAUpoi007-desc:
[{{title}}]

Were a person to travel back to the 21st century and question its inhabitants as to the projected situation of the United Nations two hundred years forward, few would have guessed that the once global organization would be hanging on to dear life in some backwater. But this is indeed the case, and Earth's finest have been stranded in New England for centuries. Children have heard stories of wars and the apocalypse from their soldier-parents, grown into adults and died while still wearing the UN insignia.

The dream of a united Earth lives on, fueled by loss and regret. Perhaps the Coasts have nothing left to lose, or perhaps, in some rusted half-sunk home is a new generation, born into poverty but kept alive by stories of a wonderful world that awaits just beyond the horizon...
NAUpoi008-desc:
[{{title}}]

During the Great Mistake, many of old America's finest fled to the Great Lakes to seek shelter from the anarchy and floods that dominated the coasts. They brought with them vast capital, giving the dying Rust Belt quick injections of cold cash and propelling the Midwest to new heights.

Today, the Great Lakes lay claim to what little remains of America's vestigial wealth. The Greater Chicago Area boasts one of the highest standards of living in the world, while Detroit is widely considered to be the manufacturing capital of the continent. Corporations can pursue their interests in peace, free from unnecessary government intervention and regulations. However, its prosperity may attract unwanted visitors, or even a full invasion...
NAUpoi009-desc:
[{{title}}]

Following the collapse of civilization on the North American continent during the latter half of the 21st century, a Great Migration began. Millions fled the coasts in panic, bringing with them children, the old, the crippled. New Englanders and Yankees settled across Pennsylvania at first, but gang tensions and famines forced another migration further West. Even today, Michigan and other Eastern states have to deal with hundreds of refugee towns. Boys have grown into men and bit the dust in these settlements, and even lowlifes call the refugee camps a cesspit. Now that tensions are rising across Central's loose domain, Chicago finds itself in the position of rare governmental unity, and can take action as needed.
NAUpoi010-desc:
[{{title}}]

The local population of this District is in a constant state of flux. Refugees from Louisiana still inhabit the Eastern coast, but regularly undergo famine as the fishing industry declines. Meanwhile, bandits and tribes from Mexico travel Northwards annually in search of more suitable climates. The recent uprising in Southern Mexico has further fueled this migration, and thousands are making their way through the border. This issue is continually destabilizing District 6 and will lend much political capital to whoever manages to resolve it.
NAUpoi011-desc:
[{{title}}]

District 6 is currently divided between ARC and Central loyalists. The former, led by Vice President Suzanne Fielding herself, consists primarily of middle-class supporters and those who stand to benefit by extensive reclamation projects along the Eastern coast. On the other end, Central loyalists are led by Axton Barron, the former representative of District 6 before his ostracization from politics in the 80s. Now, having recovered much of his political capital, Barron has returned to re-secure Texas in the name of Central. His support is primarily drawn from rich elites and power brokers who have a vested interest in attaining Central relief aid.
NAUpoi012-desc:
[{{title}}]

In the pre-Mistake era, a phrase often associated with the old United States was It can't happen here. This sentiment was for a multitude of scenarios the citizens felt would only be plausible in elaborate works of fiction; disastrous weather tearing down entire cities, American citizens killing each other in the streets, the White House and Capitol Building being stormed by soldiers to establish martial law. Then when the Great Mistake choked the skies with ash, rising tides swallowed entire states whole, militias and gangs waged violence from coast-to-coast, and the military launched the Siege of Washington in 2084, almost every concept that Americans believed couldn't happen, did happen.

While the Central government still has vestiges of the pre-Mistake branches of government, and had theoretically shed the pre-Mistake jingoism by adopting Canada and Mexico in a Greater American Identity, the national rebirth via military coup has made the Legislative and Judiciary branches rife with corruption and Machiavellian power schemes at best, and glorified rubber stamps for the President and Joint Chiefs at worst. The Executive branch, despite having the best security on the continent, routinely had their administrations prematurely ended by assassination, leading many to believe even they are but a puppet to the military, and those who don't follow the whims of their generals will have their own security turn on them like the Praetorians of Imperial Rome. Of course, how much of this is truth, and how much is anti-Central conspiracy theory, is ill-defined.

With President Cygan having finished his term in office, citing health concerns as the reason he won't run for reelection, the question of who will lead the Central government is once again open to debate. The ongoing crisis has long since thrown any elections from the common citizenry out the window, most especially after the Districts, while in theory still under Central administration, in practice became effectively independent nation-states with little loyalty paid to Central beyond the bare minimum of lip service. Thus, the Central Council—the unofficial name for the roiling sea of politicians, lobbyists, officers and spies feuding for power—is convening to select a new President, and perhaps implement some broader government reforms to salvage what little control it has left.

This could be the opportunity for the spark of democracy to reignite... or be snuffed out, once and for all.
NAUpoi013-desc:
[{{title}}]

As the leader of the Patriot Party, Luis Segerra Reyes was widely known to be President Cygan’s de facto successor after the latter declined to run for reelection. Reyes worked in the Central District as its ruling Governor, despite having only earned his citizenship status from when Central made its abortive attempt to take Mexico in the 2170s. Fiercely loyal to his newfound country, Reyes believes that the Central District represents the true legitimate authority in North America, and should be developed as the supreme capitol of a unified continent.

During his time as governor, Reyes has obtained significant influence among Central’s political and military elites. He has also attracted widespread popularity in the general public, who are taken in by his restorationist rhetoric and self-styled image as the only leader strong enough to lead their decaying nation back to its former glory. With the power of Central behind him, Reyes is determined to return America to its superpower status, no matter the cost.
NAUpoi014-desc:
[{{title}}]

Emerging as a dark horse in the race to replace Cygan, Wesley Forrest and his Elysium Party have managed to secure a surprising amount of support in the labyrinthine oligarchy of the Central Council. One of the youngest party leaders in Central’s history, Forrest grew up as part of the privileged upper class that had access to pre-Mistake history, culture, and even samples of preserved flora and fauna. More idealistic than past candidates, he wishes to restore democratic institutions in the Central government and take decisive action to regenerate America’s fading biospheres.

This platform has earned him broad approval of the masses, though it was much more pragmatic political maneuvering that carried the Elysium Party to prominence. Even so, Forrest’s ascension has made him many outspoken enemies within Central’s assorted internal cliques. Many within the Council suspect that Forrest is being puppeted by the Joint Chiefs to shore up crumbling public support and ecological conditions, and that he will be disposed of should any of his proposed reforms truly threaten their power. His own followers remain hopeful that he will yet succeed, even if it means fighting for the very soul of the NAU.
NAUpoi015-desc:
[{{title}}]

District 1 has no governing body or civilization. There are no urban cities, American suburbs, or even sustainable farms. The District's inhabitants are forced to either hunt increasingly scarce prey, vegetation, or, in more extreme instances, each other. As the District is incapable of producing its own supplies, much less its own weapons, it relies on occasional Central shipments.

Thus, as time has passed, Central has tightened its grip on the District. All ammunition inflow is possible solely through Central's approval. This new power has therefore made many successful attempts at playing the local tribes against one another. The cliques are taking over one another, completely oblivious to their position on Central's chopping block. However, immediate reconstruction of social order in District 1 is impossible. The land is ruined by poisonous gases released by warlords over the decades. Irradiated ruins still dot the plains and hills. And the survivors keep fighting...
NAUpoi016-desc:
[{{title}}]

Antony Beaton is the regional Vice President of ARC Reclamation Projects in Cascadia. Beaton began his career in 2182 as a clerk in Central government departments before moving to the East Coast in search of wider opportunities. His finances ran dry and he had to take refuge in an ARC encampment near New England. There Beaton partook in several skirmishes with raiders before being discharged from the city militias due to a festering leg wound. He would spend the next 3 years in a research hospital, where he was spared from irreparable status by undergoing a miraculous recovery.

Still recovering, Antony Beaton enlisted in the hospital staff and began a career as a research scientist. He proved his worth many times over by assisting hundreds of patients, which prompted the head doctor to recommend Beaton to his superiors in ARC itself. Beaton spent the following years studying medicine and showed an extreme interest in rejuvenation technology. He ascended the ranks at a lightning speed and was eventually assigned to lead an ARC expedition into District 2, in the hopes of flipping it to ARC's side. The Cascadian wilderness allowed Beaton to exercise his strong leadership and strategic skills. Now, Beaton has become somewhat enchanted by the enemy he is facing, the Silk Path. He makes vague promises of eternal life to his closest followers and not even ARC believes that he is a completely loyal asset anymore. However, Beaton has organized a large support base and is unlikely to stop his search.
NAUpoi017-desc:
[{{title}}]

The ARC Oversight Board is a ruling council composed of 20 members, 18 of whom are direct corporate representatives from ARC itself. Assigned to the District with the stated goal of maintaining order and reviving civilization, the Board's members have elected to build up their strength by going on vacations and purchasing the newest augmentations. ARC would do something about this insubordination, but is too preoccupied with global concerns. The Board controls the only organized military force in the District, the 68th and 45th ARC Peacekeeping Divisions.

While opposed at nearly every opportunity by local interest groups and the United Nations, the Oversight Board's power is near total. The Board commands full respect in the cities by controlling their water flow and ration intakes. While dissent is theoretically meant to be dealt with swiftly, the Board has been accused of neglecting its duties and allowing the raiders to grow out of control.
NAUpoi018-desc:
[{{title}}]

Miriam Godwinson was born in what was once Georgia, 2146. Her father was a high-ranking minister in the Evangelical Fire, one of the apocalyptic sects that appeared in local communities after the turn of the century. Baptized in River of Fire at age 7, she attended a series of religious schools, culminating in a degree in theology from the College of the Covenant and a doctorate in psychology from Newland University. By the time Godwinson began her own ministry, the Evangelical Fire was the largest Christian denomination in her home region. By the age of 26, she was the ranking Psych Priest of the Heavenly Diocese, third most senior member of the sect. In 2174, she volunteered to serve with Central Reintegration Forces sent to the North. Appointed Central District Honorary Psych Chaplain, she proved to be a talented military psychologist, but at the same time, her religious ministry to the desperate people of the region backfired.

Upon returning to the South, millions hailed her as a kind of messiah (the Prophet Phenomenon often coinciding with post-Mistake madness), forcing Central to release her from service before her presence could further inflame local religious mania. Authorities were reluctant to have such a controversial figure in a high leadership position in the District, but political pressure from the communities for the reconciling of the secular and the spiritual forced them to consider her for the position of Psych Chaplain. Her undeniable talent for that role eventually won her the appointment. Miriam is a relic of a different age. She values order and morality, and is always at odds with the march of progress. Humanity is but a child in her eyes, running from home into the great unknown.
NAUpoi019-desc:
[{{title}}]

The Great Lakes Committee is a council of local leaders, career politicians, and corporate representatives tasked with the preservation of order and steady growth in the Great Lakes District. Although initially appointed by Central in the aftermath of the 3rd American Civil War, the Committee now functions as an independent political entity. Its members are often seen as ineffectual by the wider public, but without proper elections, things are unlikely to change.
NAUpoi020-desc:
[{{title}}]

Suzanne Fielding was born the eldest of three daughters to a Mexican-born mother, and an African-American father in April, 2161. Growing up close to the Gulf Coast of Texas, she helped her father manage the three hardware stores he owned in the state—the fruits of the Central government's attempts to revitalize the region's economy after the 3rd American Civil War's so-called War of Unification. Although Central would abandon direct control of District 6 along with much of the country, Fielding exploited what opportunity was given by graduating from San Antonio's Trinity University with a double Majors in Accounting and Economics. Since then, she has made considerable progress in building a support base stretching from her native Texas to ARC itself.
NAUpoi021-desc:
[{{title}}]

Spencer Morgan began his career as an enlistee in the Central army during the early days of the 3rd Civil War. He distinguished himself by leading the famous Littletown Raid, in which he, a dozen footmen and a decrepit walker managed to break through warlord defenses and occupy Littletown, a major stronghold in the Rocky Mountains. This victory paved the way for Central domination over transportation in the mountain ranges, allowing it to operate across multiple fronts at lightning speeds. Major Morgan went on to participate in critical clashes in California and garnered much fame for his argument against the utilization of nuclear weapons against warlords there. Eventually a colonel and then a general, Spencer Morgan finished his military career at the age of 32 when he successfully pacified the warlord Dangerman in the Midwest.

For his service, General Morgan was granted authority over District 7. Exchanging the sword for the pen, Morgan proved himself a capable administrator and negotiator. He signed treaties with the local tribes and gangs, bringing much needed order to District 7. His rule saw the creation of entire cities, the resettlement of abandoned lands, and the establishment of a culture fluent in politics. Now an old man, General Morgan has mostly withdrawn from the public sphere. He spends his days secluded in his forest cabin, which has allowed bandits to resurface on the periphery. His supporters have begun to forget the man's contributions and some wonder just how strong his grip over District 7 really is.
NAUpoi022-desc:
[{{title}}]

There are many words that have been used to describe ARC's Chief Research Officer Gabriel Ivanov. Ambitious. Quirky. Antisocial. Sociopathic. Psychopathic. However, despite having almost every adjective that has existed in the English language—and a multitude of foreign language adjectives with no real equivalent in English—being used to describe Ivanov—by his admirers, his detractors, and even by himself—one word that cannot be said of him at any time is being complacent. Having effectively turned the entirety of District 8 into a glorified ARC research facility, the only real threat to Ivanov's authority is the rising sentiment of Canadian separatism that wants to stop the Firaxite Man from making their homeland his personal petri dish.
poiBRA-desc:
[{{title}}]

Brazil is a harsh military dictatorship, with its government and populace blaming all their misfortunes on the Andean Compact, their most direct neighbor, with the use of state propaganda.

The Andean Compact has on several occasions been accused of exploiting the continent, especially lithium, by moving the wealth out of it, impoverishing the rest of the countries and condemning them to hell.

Brazil believes that only through a strong reaction can the tyranny of The Andean Compact be halted.

Seeing as most of the little wealth and resources that Brazil has left has been invested in its military in anticipation of a potential war with the Compact, Brazil certainly has the capability of throwing the entire region of South America into needless conflict.
BRApoi002-desc:
[{{title}}]

Hear, hear, citizens of Brazil! The future of your great nation lays in your hands. This year will decide our fate. Shall we come together as a nation? Put aside our petty differences? Unite against hate and injustice? Shall we fight in unity against the corrupt forces of the Andean Compact?

Will you, citizen, allow your entire family to be massacred by the Andeans? Would you watch them nerve staple your children and trample on your country's flag? Go! Pick up a weapon, a spade, a hammer! Go to the front, to the factories, do not fear. When we are one - we are indestructible.
BRApoi003-desc:
[{{title}}]

In the aftermath of the 2198 coup, Manuel Branco Velho and his clique of supporters have plotted and tried everything in and beyond their power to save the regime. However, rampant deterioration of the Amazon rainforests, the collapse of order in urban centers, and the failure of the Space Campaign have taken their toll. The Brazilian people yearn for peace and accept slow rebuilding. But the regime still has an ace up its sleeve...
BRApoi004-desc:
[{{title}}]

The Brazilian army suffers from rampant unprofessionalism, with most of our rank-and-file consisting of conscripts and former criminals pressed into service. While our officer corps remain some of the best on the continent, they can only do so much when the soldiers under their command are completely lacking in discipline. If Brazil is to survive the coming war with the Compact, then these grunts must be hammered into shape.
BRApoi005: Army of Lions, Led by Lions
BRApoi005-desc:
[{{title}}]

General Rejinaldo de Alencar has always been a force for innovation within Brazil's infamously conservative military. As commander-in-chief, de Alencar intends to transform the Brazilian Armed Forces into an elite force without equal.
BRApoi006-desc:
[{{title}}]

Despite their origins as a bunch of backwoods militias, the Legião Sertão has wholeheartedly embraced Eloa Alvarez's philosophy of transhuman darwinism. Many Legionaries have enthusiastically taken to modifying themselves with combat genes, black-market bionics, and military grade cybernetics, all in the pursuit of transforming themselves into apex predators
BRApoi007-desc:
[{{title}}]

The industrialists of Brazil have always been supportive of Frederico Watanabe's free market policies, especially compared to the stifling dirigisme of the military regime. Many prominent businessmen followed Watanabe into exile after the Coup of '98, and have remained close allies of the president upon his return to Brazil.
BRApoi008-desc:
[{{title}}]

Although it is the democratically elected government of Brazil, many remain unconvinced that President Watanabe is anything more than an Andean puppet. The fact that the Brazilian administration has spent two years in exile in Lima has only strengthened this notion, not to mention the fact that they are still reliant on Andean aid.

To regain the support of the people, they will need to demonstrate that its forces fight for liberty and democracy rather than foreign interests. They have to prove that the legitimate government can stand on its own two feet and fight for its people.
BRApoi009-desc:
[{{title}}]

The Lamentadores have spent decades fighting a guerilla war against the Brazilian state in what remains of the Amazon jungle. Although the clique was founded with lofty ideals in mind, years of non-stop insurgency have pushed it further and further from its idealistic origins. They walk a fine line between crusading a noble cause and giving to brutal pragmatism.

Right now, the people view the Lamentadores as little more than terrorists. Its forces are merciless, and it still relies on underworld contacts to keep the lights on. While its enemies fear them, so do the Brazilian people. The Lamentadores are a long way from cementing their image as a legitimate force for good in Brazil
BRApoi010-desc:
[{{title}}]

General Manuel Branco Velho had always stood apart from the rest of Brazil's military elite. Where most commissioned officers were the sons of generals and oligarchs, Velho enjoyed no such privilege as the fourth son of a Cuiabá handyman. Like many in the favelas, Velho and his brothers left for the army at a young age in pursuit of a better life.

During the Cerrado War, Velho lost all but one of his brothers in the war against the guerillas, yet gained a reputation as a model soldier who never flinched in the face of the enemy. His heroic actions during Operation Navalha caught the attention of his commanding officers, who then acted as his patrons during his rise to the Brazilian High Command during the 2170's.

An avowed Brazilian nationalist, General Velho was the driving force behind the Coup of '98 that overthrew President Frederico Watanabe for his connections with the Andean Compact. Declaring a state of emergency soon after, he then focused on restoring the prominence of the Brazilian Armed Forces in preparation for the eventual war with the Compact, claiming them to be both the main threat Brazilian sovereignty and the main obstacle to Brazilian prosperity.

While his critics paint Velho as yet another opportunistic dictator, he maintains that he has always been a man who has stopped at nothing in service of his fatherland. Everything that General Velho has done has been in the name of reasserting Brazil's status as a global power by any means necessary.
BRApoi011-desc:
[{{title}}]

It was once said, that the first person who will live 150 years has already been born. There are more than a few who think that Ximenes will hold that title. Born in Brazil during the Dark Age, Ximenes grew up seeing the consequences of humanity's destruction of the environment first hand. Once he came of age, he took a job in academia, travelling across South America, learning of the continent's rich culture and history. He had hoped that through this scholarship, the solution for mankind's failure could be found. He was wrong. Years of travel and research made him realise that Brazil needed more than philosophers to save the Amazon. That was when he met Eloa Alvarez.

Alvarez grew fond of such an educated man, and brought Ximenes into their survivalists group of insurgents who sought to preserve the Amazon through action not words. For a time, Ximenes went along with this group and happily helped in their mission. But as the years went on, he began to see Alvarez not as a liberator, but a semi-fascist autocrat. With a heart heavy from the many crimes he had committed, Ximenes deserted the group, taking many like minded followers with him.

Ximenes spent the next few decades forming his own survivalist militia, revealing himself as a gentle man with a kind heart. Many flocked to his side, viewing Ximenes as the best chance for Brazil to save itself. Both culturally and ecologically. Emphasised by his reluctance to use the under handed tactic used by other factions. But now, at over a century old, and a chance to realise his dream for a green Brazil here, it is feared he will not live to see it. The young man that once led entire platoons of soldiers and guerrillas can now only walk with the assistance of a cane. Even the advanced medicine and technology of this era give him a few decades of life at the most. With the Grim Reaper fast approaching, Ximenes plans to use his skills as much as he can. So that when he finally does depart from this world, it will be a better place than when he entered it.
BRApoi012-desc:
[{{title}}]

Eloa Alvarez is yet another leader among the many figures of South America, but even among the harsh survivalists of the region, she is notorious for her rigid beliefs, staunch belief in might-makes-right, and a fearsome military.

The military in question is composed mostly of fellow survivalists- they are drawn to power like moths, and Eloa bears the torch of strength. Even for them her practices are brutal, and this brutality enforces her will over theirs. Survivalists are loyal, but that loyalty is only to power. A sign of weakness, and the warriors may leave to stronger rulers still- or deem themselves stronger instead. Survivalists are both a source of strength, and what tests it. Often, signs of mercy may be a weakness in the eyes of those who find mercy an alien thing, and there will be time for mercy once the work is done.

Her history is usually kept private- she sees no reason to share it- but it is generally understood she grew up among the lower classes along the northern outskirts of Brazil, the tumultuous border regions of her country. Raiders, bandits, and survivalists often raided her home, making each day a question of life and death. Her father was the only notable figure in her life, an old soldier who fought in a forgotten war. Despite his efforts, his beliefs contrasted with what Eloa saw—and she saw violence.

Violence breeds violence, and the womb of war bred something far worse than petty thieves and lost warriors robbing families—it bore Alvarez, and at her command was all the horrors her army could muster.

She was borne by the sword, and was forced to live by it, and now she must ensure no other weapon may pose a threat to her people, her people of many blades.
